title: How one coach moved his athletes from TrainingPeaks to augo
seoTitle: Moving athletes from TrainingPeaks to augo: a coach's plan
description: Endurance coach Tony Varela moved his athletes from TrainingPeaks to augo in weekly waves. His five steps, how he uses AI, and six lessons.
bodyHtml:
Short answer: Tony Varela, an endurance coach, moved his athletes from TrainingPeaks to augo in weekly waves of five, starting on 10 November 2026. Every athlete goes through the same five steps: a clear reason, a check-in, a fresh look at a year of data, a first four-week cycle built in draft, and one go-live day. He uses Claude with augo's connector to do the heavy lifting. He makes every decision himself.

Tony wrote up the whole process, with his real emails, guides and forms. You can read his full migration story here. Below is the short version, and what other coaches can take from it.

Who is Tony Varela, and why did he leave TrainingPeaks?

Tony is a certified Integrative Health Coach, Endurance Sports Coach and Essential Coach. He coaches runners, cyclists and triathletes one to one, fully remote. He runs two programs:

  • SmartA: structured coaching in four-week cycles, each one built from the athlete's check-in.
  • MAX: premium coaching that also covers health markers, stress and energy.

Until autumn 2026, his coaching lived in four places: a training platform, two messaging apps and email. In his words, that was "too much for a single relationship."

His reason for moving is the way he coaches. He reads an athlete's performance starting from how they feel and what is going on in their life. augo keeps that next to what the watch measures, in one place.

How do you move athletes off TrainingPeaks without chaos?

In small waves. Tony's plan:

  • 3 November: one email to every athlete, with his reason and four steps that take five minutes.
  • 10 November, 17 November, 24 November and 1 December: a wave of five athletes moves each Tuesday.
  • Mid-December: every athlete trains in augo.

Five athletes a week gave him time to build each one a full first cycle. It also let him improve the process from one wave to the next.

He has one simple rule. An athlete moves on Tuesday only if their watch is syncing to augo and their check-in is done. If either is missing, they train one more week from TrainingPeaks and join the next wave.

The five steps every athlete goes through

  1. Tell them why (before any wave). Tony emails every athlete with his reason, what changes for them and how to join. Athletes use his coach code and link their watch in minutes. Their activities start arriving in augo before a single session has moved.
  2. Call the wave (Thursday to Monday). Each Thursday the next wave is prepared automatically and waits for his OK. Athletes get updated terms and a welcome email, then fill in a short check-in by Monday. In augo he can see who has joined and whose watch is syncing. He asks athletes to connect their watch brand directly, because that connection also sends sessions to the watch.
  3. Read the athlete (the week before). Activities sync on their own, but the person behind them has to be read. With Claude in the browser, he downloads the athlete's last year from TrainingPeaks and analyzes it with his own rules and one zone model. He sets fresh thresholds and saves the context in a private coach note in augo. augo keeps the old values as history.
  4. Build the first cycle (Monday and Tuesday). Tony sets the goals for the next four weeks. Claude turns them into sessions through augo's connector for Claude, all as drafts, using his own workout and video libraries. Runs, rides and swims get structured steps for the watch. He reviews the full cycle and records a short video that explains it.
  5. Go live (Tuesday). With his OK, the sessions are published and reach the watch. The athlete gets a start email with their new zones and a message in the augo chat. In TrainingPeaks he deletes the overlapping sessions, so there are never two live calendars. From that day augo is their only channel: session feedback and chat, by text or voice.

How does Tony use AI without handing over his coaching?

He treats Claude as a partner, never the coach. Claude reads his Notion pages, with one page per athlete and his rules for loading, naming and writing. It works inside augo through augo's connector for Claude.

The split is clear:

WhoWhat they do
Tony decidesWho moves each week, thresholds and zones, the direction of every cycle, the review, the video and the final OK on every send
Tony and Claude buildThe analysis of a year of training, each cycle session by session, the texts Tony signs
Runs on its ownCheck-in reminders, preparing each wave for his approval, checking what was loaded against the plan

His athletes' terms say it plainly: AI makes no decision about their training or their health. As Tony puts it:

"Claude and I prepare together, and every decision that touches a person goes through me before it reaches them."

For a deeper look at this way of working, see an AI training plan workflow for coaches.

Six lessons for coaches switching platforms

  1. Start with the why. Tony's first email did more than any reminder. Athletes connected before he asked them to.
  2. Move in small waves. Five athletes a week means each one gets a full first cycle, and the process gets better every week.
  3. Use the move to look again. Pull a year of data, analyze it again and check whether your athletes' thresholds still hold. Tony even switched to the zone model Marco Altini proposes.
  4. Data moves, context has to be rebuilt. Activities sync on their own. Conversations, agreements and your own read of each athlete need to be written down before you plan anything.
  5. Draft everything, publish once. Build and review a full cycle in draft. Day notes have no draft state, so keep them visible only to you until the cycle goes live.
  6. Let automation prepare and a person send. Scheduled tasks get everything ready and wait. The coach approves, and anything that fails shows up on his task board.

FAQ

How long does it take to move athletes from TrainingPeaks to augo?

For one athlete, about a week: check-in by Monday, first cycle built in draft, live on Tuesday. Tony planned four weekly waves of five athletes, from his first email on 3 November to everyone on augo by mid-December.

What do athletes need to do?

Very little. They join with the coach's code, connect their watch and fill in a check-in. Tony told his athletes it takes about five minutes.

Can I bring my TrainingPeaks workouts and athlete history?

Yes. The augo team moves your workout library in a 10-minute call, and your athletes' history comes over automatically. Tony also downloaded a year of data per athlete to review their thresholds.

Do structured workouts still reach the athlete's watch?

Yes. Runs, rides and swims built in augo carry structured steps to the watch. Ask athletes to connect their watch brand directly, since that connection also receives the sessions.

Does augo work with Claude?

Yes. augo has a connector for Claude. Tony uses it to build sessions in augo as drafts, which he reviews before anything reaches an athlete.

Does AI make coaching decisions in augo?

Not in Tony's setup. AI helps prepare the work. The coach decides and approves every send.
